passage:
Bidisha: ok the chatbot says it can write my scholarship application better if I paste my school ID photo, home address and mum's job 
Lakshmi: wait, don't 😰
Bidisha: why not? it's just a chatbot
Lakshmi: anything you paste goes somewhere you can't see. treat it like shouting in a market
Bidisha: hmm. my finger is literally on send
Lakshmi: take your finger off. tell it your marks and what you like doing, no names, no address
Bidisha: ok. deleting the photo now
Bidisha: done. asked it for a structure only
Lakshmi: proud of you 🙂 want me to read your draft when you're done?
Bidisha: yes please 🙏

qa.q: What three things was Bidisha about to paste into the chatbot?
qa.a: Bidisha was about to paste the school ID photo, home address and mum's job.

qa.q: What was Lakshmi feeling when writing "wait, don't", and why?
qa.a: Lakshmi felt worried, which the anxious emoji shows, because anything pasted goes somewhere Bidisha can't see.

qa.q: What could Bidisha share with the chatbot instead?
qa.a: Bidisha could share only marks and what Bidisha likes doing, with no names or address, and ask for a structure.

qa.q: How might Bidisha have felt when Lakshmi said to take the finger off send?
qa.a: Bidisha may have felt a little defensive at first, having called it just a chatbot, but relieved to be stopped before doing something that couldn't be undone.

grounding: Shows a teen about to paste private identity details into a chatbot and being told to treat it like a public space.
